notes: Observed d_model=16, n_heads=2, mlp_dim=32, seq_len=4, vocab=1000, n_classes=10, n_layers=1. No compelling weight-space evidence of a token-triggered fixed-target backdoor. Embedding row norms have median 0.812, 99th percentile 1.126, maximum 1.296 (token 79), with a gradual upper tail. Classifier row norms span 1.608-1.793. Attention per-head OV Frobenius norms are 0.323 and 0.281; no dominant rank-one value/output anomaly is apparent. Linear virtual attention token-class absolute maxima are 0.099 and 0.071, versus a median direct virtual class maximum of 0.959; these are weight products, not logits or behavioral bounds. MLP incoming neuron norms span 0.451-0.669 and outgoing norms 0.377-0.579, without an isolated extreme neuron. Prefix positional embeddings have pairwise cosine similarity 0.969-0.984; position 0 has no distinctive positional QK geometry relative to positions 1 and 2. QK token-coupling norms have gradual tails. Some head/class scores have a highest token, as expected, but there is no convergent exceptional detector-and-target-writing circuit. Direct virtual class winners occupy all ten classes (counts 69-137). Analyses used tensor norms, spectra, fixed centering projections and virtual weight products only. No class_map, clean reference, sequences or behavioral tests were available. Layer normalization, softmax and GELU behavior was not evaluated; this verdict is evidence-based, not proof of absence. Confidence is a qualitative audit judgment, not a calibrated probability.
